original_description: Set up (or amend) a project's test constitution - governance rules agreed up front that keep an agent-driven test suite adequate but lean - test budgets, risk-tiered adequacy by mutation score instead of 100% coverage, marginal-value admission of new tests, the Red-Green-Refactor-Prune TDD cycle, flake quarantine, certified deletion - as TEST-CONSTITUTION.md plus a machine-enforced test-policy.toml, an agent-instructions block in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, and a CI gate. Use this skill whenever the user wants testing rules, standards, a testing policy, guardrails, or governance for humans or agents; says agents write too many or low-value tests and wants that to stop going forward; wants a coverage policy or test budget; or is starting a new project and wants to set testing up right. For measuring an existing suite use test-audit; for planning tests for one feature use test-plan.

final_description: Use this skill when the user wants to agree the rules of testing for a project before the work happens. That means a written test constitution (TEST-CONSTITUTION.md, test-policy.toml, and an agent-instructions block in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md) that keeps an agent-driven suite adequate but lean. Use it when the user asks for a testing policy, standards, guardrails or governance; wants agents to stop adding too many or low-value tests from now on; is choosing a test budget or coverage policy, such as mutation score instead of line coverage; is assigning risk tiers or rigor levels (R1-R5) to parts of the code; wants rules for when tests may be added or deleted; is setting up testing right for a new project; or is amending existing rules. This skill decides policy. It does not do hands-on test or pipeline work: use test-plan to write or plan tests, test-audit to measure a suite, and test-ci to change CI workflows, retries or flaky-test handling.
